Howling north wind and lightning filled the night as pine trees swayed and some fell. The storm was incredibly loud, and there was no mistaking when conditions went from bad to ten times worse. The roaring winds intensified dramatically, and at that point, we made sure to stay well away from doors and windows. The doors shook so violently that it sounded as though someone was repeatedly pounding on them, trying to get inside. At times, I genuinely thought they might burst open. It felt and sounded like the house was breathing. 

Countless fences went down. Somewhere in the woods behind my property, what appeared to be part of someone's roof or porch was blown into the trees. By morning, the smell of freshly cut pine filled the air.

Final 8:00 a.m. measured reading (Oct. 10): 6.63 inches.
